text:
elaine: Heads up — incoming escalations from two customers in us-west: /v1/embeddings p99 jumped from ~120ms -> ~1.2s after Friday night changes. p95 up ~2x. No consistent 5xxs but some 502s observed. Dashboard: https://redwood.app/d/embeds/us-west (embedding latency chart). Anyone oncall?

sandeep: I'm on it. Looking at traces now. Spans show auth-proxy waiting on metadata/kv lookups and backend TCP waits. Traces: auth-proxy -> kv-store (tcp handshake, 200-600ms).

marc: Noticed we did the CUDA/driver rollout Friday 23:40 for us-west (driver 535.22). Ops notes show concurrent node reboots and nvme firmware flashes on some hosts.

rachel: Customer said they were sending larger batch sizes (batch=32) around the time. Could make tails worse.

elaine: Customer impact: 2 mid-market customers on dedicated capacity, affecting embeddings-heavy endpoints (batching jobs). They've escalated to support.

sandeep: Quick datapoints:
- tcp retransmits high on backend connections from proxy -> kv nodes
- iostat on affected inference hosts shows high await and long write latency to /dev/nvme0n1
- kernel dmesg shows nvme timeouts around the same window

marc: Paste from one affected host (short):
```
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s     rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.00   45.00  102400.00 204800.00  6144.00  12.34  120.56  8.12  130.44  1.75  85.34
```
(awwwait numbers spiking to >100ms during incident window)

rachel: That aligns with a storage I/O contention story. If auth-proxy depends on KV writes for token introspect/caching, slow NVMe could push proxy spans into tail latency, especially under large batches.

elaine: Repro steps for us:
1) Send embedding requests with batch=32 to us-west (curl example):
```
curl -s -w "HTTP_T=%{time_total}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood/test/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-l16","input":["x"] * 32}'
```
2) Run tcpdump between proxy and kv-node while load runs:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host kv-node-ip and port 6379 -w /tmp/kv.pcap
```
3) Collect dmesg and iostat on inference host.

sandeep: Short-term mitigations applied:
- rolled auth-proxy back to v1.18.3 (previous) at 1759123700 — started seeing tail drop immediately for some customers (dashboard shows p99 down ~30%). ops-bot will post deploy log.
- recommended customers reduce max batch to 16 as temporary mitigation
- enabled local in-memory token cache on proxy to reduce KV trips (config flip: PROXY_TOKEN_CACHE=true)

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled back service "auth-proxy" from 1.19.0 -> 1.18.3 in us-west at 1759123700. CI job: deploy/rollback/3821.

marc: From infra triage: driver 535.22 appears correlated with nvme latency spikes on ~8 hosts. Vendor bug suspected: async flush path stalls under concurrent kernel NVMe queue depth + heavy DMA from GPU kernels. Workaround options: pin to 535.17 or apply host kernel nvme timeout patch.

rachel: Filed internal infra issue INC-7891 and vendor bug report (case #VND-4321). Notifying customers with mitigation steps.

elaine: Next steps and owners:
- sandeep: validate proxy rollback across all affected clusters + measure p99 (owner)
- marc: coordinate rollback/pin of GPU driver on impacted hosts, and schedule deeper host-level bisect (owner)
- rachel: customer comms + recommend reduced batch + track support tickets (owner)
- infra: check nvme firmware versions and consider firmware backports (owner: marc)

sandeep: Quick note — if we can't roll back driver fleet-wide quickly, we should increase KV timeouts on proxy and add circuit-breaker to avoid blocking RPS. Also consider moving auth token checks to local JWT validation to cut KV dependency.

marc: Agreed. For now, pinning driver on the 8 noisy hosts to 535.17 and rebooting reduced NVMe await back to normal on 6/8. Two hosts show persistent tail and are in deeper debug.

elaine: Customer update draft: "We identified a storage I/O interaction tied to a recent driver rollout + auth-proxy change that increased tail latency for embeddings. We have rolled back the proxy and applied mitigations; we are pinning drivers and continuing investigation. We will follow up with a post-incident summary."

rachel: Adding a perf regression test to CI: run embed batch=32 1k reqs, assert p99 < 500ms. Ticket created: ENG-PT-1122.

ops-bot: incident-bot: created incident report INC-7891 and assigned severity P2. Links: https://redwood.incidents/INC-7891

elaine: Thanks everyone — I'll coordinate the customer calls and close the support escalations once p99 is back to baseline.

marc: I'll continue host bisect and share kernel/dmesg snippets in the incident thread.

sandeep: Leaving notes here too: consider adding a kv-prefetch path and make token validation resilient to kv spikes.

rachel: Good catch all, keep updates short. :thumbsup:
